proof_summary: For an odd prime \(p\) and \(t\ge2\), counting the factors \(2^{jd}-1\), where \(d=\operatorname{ord}_p(2)\mid p-1\), and comparing their \(p\)-adic contribution with that of \((pt-1)!\) shows \(p\mid a(pt-1)\); thus a proper odd prime divisor of \(n\) would force \(p\mid2^{n-2}\), while \(v_2(a(2^v-1))=v-1\) excludes the remaining composite case \(n=2^v\). Once \(n\) is prime, if \(d=\operatorname{ord}_n(2)<n-1\), then the factor \(2^d-1\) makes \(n\) divide the numerator but not \((n-1)!\), forcing \(n\mid a(n-1)\) and hence \(n\mid2^{n-2}\), a contradiction; therefore \(d=n-1=\varphi(n)\).
